terra.problem: The reference to shepherds in the Christmas story is a Bible fact outside this passage and needs a reference.
The explanation is generic and repetitive, with little of Papa Dorin's personality.
The explanation is flat and generic; the closing line adds no distinct personality.
The joke depends on knowing that Papa wanted to keep his name, but it gives the baker no context for that part of his story.
The guest-list line implies that nobody is excluded. Simeon says salvation was prepared in the sight of all people, not that everyone is included on a guest list.
Simeon says the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed, not that the hearts themselves will be revealed.
Asher is identified as Anna's tribe, not as a place where her family came from.
The passage does not say Anna was not asked to act or that she thanked God for the Child. It says she gave thanks and spoke about Him.
The passage does not say they went straight home or took no scenic route.
The passage names their destination but does not say there were no detours.
The passage says the Child grew and was filled with wisdom; it does not say here that His wisdom grew.
